 From life to life, F. S. plays with the concept of reincarnation throughout the poem; he is born again
as Ariel, who was himself formerly imprisoned in a pine tree, just as was the guitar, fashioned from pine
wood. S. in the poem thus identifies also with the guitar, making his gift to Jane a symbol of himself as
the giver. Pythagoreanism, mediated through Platonic texts, promoted the doctrine of metempsychosis
or the transmigration of souls which, themselves immortal, live in successive physical incarnations. The
ideas would have been long familiar to S., but perhaps newly interesting in light of the Anglo-Indian
background of his immediate circle in Pisa, who may have discussed reincarnation in Hinduism; cp.,
